implemented_requirements.evidence: Match3Game._fill_board creates self.board as a 2‑D list of colour codes (game.py, lines 31‑35).
Match3Game.swap exchanges two cells; Match3Game.is_valid_move checks adjacency (abs(r1‑r2)+abs(c1‑c2)==1) (game.py, lines 45‑55).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect matches of three or more
implemented_requirements.evidence: Match3Game.find_matches scans rows and columns for runs >=3 and returns a set of coordinates (game.py, lines 57‑78).
Match3Game.resolve sets matched cells to None, builds a stack of remaining candies per column, drops them down and fills empty slots with new random candies (game.py, lines 84‑99).
In resolve, after dropping, empty positions are filled with self.rng.choice(COLORS) (game.py, line 98).
self.score is increased by points returned from resolve; points are calculated as len(matches)*20*cascade (game.py, lines 84‑92). UI displays score (ui.py, line 15).
self.moves_left initialized to DEFAULT_MOVES (20) and decremented in move(); over() ends game when moves_left <= 0 (game.py, lines 33, 108‑110). UI shows moves left (ui.py, line 13).
resolve() loops while new matches appear, incrementing cascade counter and applying additional points (game.py, lines 84‑95). UI reports cascades (ui.py, lines 61‑66).
ui.find_hint scans for any valid move and returns a suggestion (ui.py, lines 30‑38).
move() calls self.shuffle() if has_any_move() is false; shuffle creates a new random board without immediate matches (game.py, lines 102‑111). UI notifies player (ui.py, line 71).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Win condition based on target score
implemented_requirements.evidence: TARGET_SCORE constant (1500) and final check in ui.main() prints win message if game.score >= TARGET_SCORE (ui.py, lines 73‑78).

judge.summary: The submitted code provides a complete, runnable match‑3 game. It implements board generation, adjacency swaps, match detection, clearing with gravity, refilling, scoring, move limits, chain reactions, shuffling when stuck, and a terminal UI with hints and win/lose messages. No missing core functionality or unimplemented stubs are observed, and the code appears ready to execute.
